meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start with who decided that and when.
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. On what basis was the zero entered?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
Show me where it appears in Owen's essay, and the cited act and scene. And did you ask Owen about that line before you entered the zero, Hale?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. "It seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down word for word, and the principal will be reading it today.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn and that nothing about this essay is placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with nothing agreed and the principal now involved.
What moved her: nothing, though the owned phone call and the misquoted Hamlet line had started to earn small ground before the remark about Claire undid it.
